blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: We trained Agaram 2.5B, a 2.5-billion-parameter Tamil-English language model, from scratch on about 50 billion tokens (58% Tamil, the rest English, math, code and parallel text) on one node of eight H100 GPUs in about six days, with a new tokenizer that, unlike our first model's, keeps line breaks. Supervised fine-tuning on 134,428 conversations, whose replies an open-weight teacher model wrote, and three short targeted rounds turned it into a chat model that answers in Tamil script, romanized Tamil (Tanglish) and English and can call tools: on 25 tool prompts whose schemas appear in training it picks the right tool 23 times and gives exactly the expected arguments 13 times. The released model translates better than Sarvam-1, a 2B Indic base model, in all six FLORES and IN22 directions (FLORES chrF 54.3 into Tamil and 55.2 into English, against 49.2 and 44.2), and nearly doubles its base model on native-Tamil IndicIFEval (19.3% from 10.0%). It is weak on knowledge: reading-comprehension and knowledge benchmarks sit near chance, and on 50 held-out everyday questions written by one native speaker, one LLM judge rated 46% of its replies usable (22-24 of 50 over three passes; 95% interval for 23 of 50, 33-60%), with nearly every failure a wrong fact. Our two further SFT experiments changed answer format but not the knowledge measures. We also describe our first model, Agaram 1.5B, whose failures shaped the choices here; how the judge's scores varied between passes on identical replies; and, item by item, what the targeted rounds trained against and where frontier-model text entered the data. The project ran on compute credits and our own funds, about USD 13,300 across both models; the weights are released (licence to be announced after legal review), with GGUF files for llama.cpp, at https://huggingface.co/murai-labs/agaram-2.5b-instruct; code at https://github.com/Murai-Labs/Agaram2.5b
blocks.zh: 我们训练了Agaram 2.5B, 一个25亿参数的泰米尔-英语语言模型, 从头到尾的大约500亿个信使(58%泰米尔, 其余的英语,数学,代码和平行文本), 在大约6天的时间里, 监督134,428个对话的微调,这些对话的回答是开放式的教师模型所写的,三个简短的定向回合将它变成了一个聊天模式,用泰米尔文、罗马化的泰米尔文(英语)和英文回答,并且可以调用工具:在25个工具提示上,其计划出现在培训中,它选择了正确的工具23次,并给出了13次预期的论据。 发布模型比Sarvam-1,一个2B Indic基准模型翻译得更好,在所有六个FLORES和IN22方向(FLORES chrF 54.3为泰米尔语,55.2为英语,对49.2和44.2),几乎是本土-Tamil Indicaleval基准模型的两倍(19.3%为10.0%)。 在知识方面它很薄弱:阅读-理解和知识基准几乎是偶然的,在一位讲母语的人每天写的50个被搁置的问题上,一位LLM法官将46%的答复评为可用(50分之三的22-24分;23分之33-60%的间隔为95%),几乎每一次失败都是错误的事实。 我们的另外两个SFT实验改变了答案格式,但并没有改变知识措施。 我们还描述了我们的第一个模型Agaram 1.5B, 其失败决定了这里的选择; 法官的得分如何在相同答复上出现差异; 以及逐个项目, 所训练的定向子弹, 以及边界模型文本输入数据的地方。 该项目使用计算入计量和我们自己的资金,大约13,300美元。 两种模型的权重(许可证在法律审查后公布)公布,GGUF文件为lama.cpp,见https://huggingface.co/murai-labs/agaram-2.5b-instruct;代码见https://github.com/Murai-Labs/Agaram2.5b。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Tamil has tens of millions of speakers and a literature more than two thousand years old, and much of its everyday
digital use is in romanized form, Tanglish. Open language models serve it poorly, and part of the reason is mechanical.
A model reads text as tokens, pieces of words drawn from a fixed vocabulary that is learned mostly from English. On our
samples, Qwen2.5’s tokenizer splits an average Tamil word into 9.4 tokens but an English word into 1.35
(Table 2 ). For the same number of words, a Tamil text there needs about seven times as many tokens as an
English one, so it fills the model’s context about seven times as fast and costs more to train on and to generate. For a small model trained
on a small budget, that cost decides what is possible.

blocks.en:
We built \tamilfont அகரம் / Agaram 2.5B to see what a small model can do when it is designed for Tamil from the start. It is trained
from scratch: its weights start from random values, not from another model, and its tokenizer was trained on our own
mix of Tamil, English, code and chat text, so a Tamil word costs 1.55 tokens. We pretrained it on about 50 billion
tokens, 58% of them Tamil, on one node of eight H100 GPUs in six days, then fine-tuned it on 134,428 conversations and
three short rounds aimed at specific failures. The released model answers in Tamil script, Tanglish and English and
calls tools: on the 25 tool prompts of our second evaluation set, whose tool schemas also appear in training, it chose
the right tool 23 times and gave exactly the expected arguments 13 times. It translates better than Sarvam-1, a 2B model trained on many Indian languages, in all six directions we
measured, but it is weak on knowledge: an LLM judge rated about half of its answers to everyday questions usable.
Figure 1 shows the whole pipeline with its numbers.

blocks.en:
Training from scratch costs more than adapting an existing model, and we chose it for two reasons. An adapted model
keeps the tokenizer of its parent, and with it the token cost above; adding Tamil tokens to the vocabulary lowers the
cost, but the new tokens start untrained inside a model that learned its language from the old ones. And with a model trained from scratch we know every document it has seen, which
is what makes the contamination checks in this report possible: before we report a benchmark score we check whether
the benchmark’s text was in our training data. Three further choices run through the work. The assistant replies in
our generated training data were written by open-weight models; frontier models such as Claude and Codex helped plan
the work and write code and may write the user side of a conversation, but not the replies the model learns from
(Section 7.2 lists the one place this was not followed). The evaluation sets we report are checked against the
training data before their numbers are reported, except four benchmarks we name (Section 7 ). And because a single pass of an LLM judge over the same
replies moved by up to 11 points, chat quality is reported as a mean over several passes with its range
(Section 8.2 ).

The report describes the full recipe at a scale a student team can reproduce. Section 2 explains why we
built the model and what our first model taught us. Sections 3 and 4 cover the tokenizer,
the data and a pretraining run that finished in one attempt. Section 5 evaluates the base model on public
Tamil benchmarks, and Section 7 checks those benchmarks against the training data.
Section 6 describes fine-tuning, including two negative results: three targeted rounds improved the probe items
they aimed at but made no difference we could detect in chat quality on prompts they never saw (22.3 against 21.0 of
50), and two further experiments changed the form of the answers but did not improve the knowledge measures. Section 8 reports the released
model, with a held-out chat set written by a native speaker and its known failures, and Section 9 the
cost.

blocks.en:
By a Tamil-first model we mean one for which Tamil is the majority of its pretraining
tokens; \tamilfont அகரம் / Agaram 2.5B’s are 58% Tamil. Most open Tamil models adapt an existing model; Tamil-LLaMA, for example,
continues Llama 2 with 16,000 added Tamil tokens [ 6 ] . Models trained from scratch that
include Tamil are mostly multilingual. Sarvam-1 (about 2B parameters, ten Indic languages and English, about 4 trillion
tokens) is a base model [ 19 ] . Sarvam 30B and 105B are trained from scratch, cover the 22 scheduled
Indian languages and support tool calling [ 20 ] ; both are mixture-of-experts models, and the
30B model activates 2.4B parameters per token, close to our 2.5B. BharatGen’s Param2, also a mixture of experts (17B
total, 2.4B active), covers English and the 22 scheduled languages and supports tool calling [ 8 ] ;
its predecessor PARAM-1 (2.9B) was trained from scratch on Hindi and English [ 17 ] . Paramanu trains monolingual models from scratch for five Indian
languages including Tamil, at 108M to 367M parameters [ 15 ] . The closest work to ours is Balaji V’s
1111AI-Tamil1B, released on 9 October 2026 [ 7 ] : a Tamil-first model trained from scratch with
1.24B parameters (1.12B without embeddings), pretrained on Tamil, Tanglish and English text (57.6B tokens seen) and
instruction-tuned on 11,261 question–answer pairs; its card states that it has no tool use. Smaller Tamil models trained from
scratch include GPT2-Tamil [ 1 ] and a 23M-parameter model [ 2 ] . As far as we know, as of 12 October 2026, \tamilfont அகரம் / Agaram 2.5B is the first
Tamil-first model trained from scratch that does tool calling. It is also, to our knowledge, the largest openly released
Tamil-first model trained from scratch.

blocks.en: 2.1 Why Agaram
blocks.zh: 2.1 国家 为什么阿加兰

blocks.en:
The first books I remember are copies of \tamilfont அம்புலிமாமா (Ambulimama) my father brought home, and I still connect them
with the smell of coffee, idli and sambar. My favourite part was \tamilfont வேதாளம் சொல்லும் கதை, the Vikram and Vetal
stories. Every story ends with a question the king has to answer, and he cannot stay silent if he knows the answer.
Through stories like these, and the other Tamil books my father kept bringing, I came to love the language and to feel I
owed something to the generations who had kept it alive for more than two thousand years.

blocks.en:
When I started working with language models, a question followed me: what would a model learn if Tamil guided it from
the first token, with a tokenizer built for Tamil, data chosen for Tamil, and training from scratch rather than borrowed
from an English model? The question became personal when I thought of my nephews and nieces. They will grow up asking
machines questions, writing with them and learning from them. I want them to be able to do that in Tamil, as naturally
as I read those books. I cannot accept a future in which those tools work well only in English.

blocks.en:
So I tried. It started as a personal project: I began collecting data in December 2025 and wrote the first code in May
2026, and it kept growing. My earlier experiments had taught me how to build a language model, but Tamil was a different
problem. Open Tamil datasets are few and small. Older writing is scarcer still: Project Madurai’s whole collection of
digitised Tamil texts comes to about 45 million tokens, under a tenth of a percent of what \tamilfont அகரம் / Agaram 2.5B was trained
on, and everything written in Tamil before 1900 that has been digitised would fit on a thumb drive. The language has
also changed: the Tamil of those texts is far from the Tamil people speak and type today, which mixes in English and is
often written in Latin script.

In June 2026 two volunteers, Madhusudhanan G and Kaushik Kezendirane, joined, and from then on it was our project. I
built in public and posted weekly updates, and many people wrote in to support the work or offer help. That is when I

\tamilfont அகரம் / Agaram 2.5B is the result. As far as we know, at the time of writing it is the first model trained from scratch with
Tamil as its primary language that does tool calling, and the largest such model openly released
(Section 1 lists the closest work). It is a small model with real gaps, which this report sets out, and we
release it, with everything we learned, so that the larger Tamil models that follow do not have to start where we did.
The books my father gave me made Tamil part of my life. I hope this work helps Tamil remain part of the tools the next
generation grows up with.

blocks.en: 2.2 The first model
blocks.zh: 2.2 国家 第一个模型

blocks.en: Figure 2 shows how the two models were built over five months.
blocks.zh: 图2显示两种模型在5个月内的构建情况。

blocks.en:
We began in May 2026 planning a hybrid of Mamba and attention layers. Mamba is a
state-space layer: it processes a sequence in time that grows linearly with its length, where attention grows with the
square of the length, so a hybrid promised longer contexts for the same compute, which matters on a small budget. The
risk is quality, so we set a rule before training anything: a hybrid would replace the standard Transformer only if it
matched or beat the Transformer on held-out Tamil text and was also more efficient on long contexts. We tested it at small scale with a ladder of models of about
91M parameters, three random seeds each, trained for up to 75,000 steps (about 154M tokens) and scored on 1,400 held-out
Tamil records in five registers. At 25,000 steps a hybrid with Mamba-2 layers matched the dense Transformer (held-out
loss 6.891 ± 0.011 6.891\pm 0.011 against 6.901 ± 0.006 6.901\pm 0.006 , mean and standard deviation over three seeds, lower is better). At
75,000 steps the dense model was clearly ahead ( 7.003 ± 0.055 7.003\pm 0.055 against 7.278 ± 0.078 7.278\pm 0.078 ), even though the Mamba-2

blocks.en:
From late May to the end of June we assembled the first corpus: Tamil web crawls (FineWeb-2,
HPLT, Sangraha) and the text of Tamil books from TamilBooksPDF and Archive.org. Much printed Tamil exists only as scanned
images, so we ran Tesseract OCR over the Tamil Digital Library and the scanned part of the TamilBooksPDF collection. By 17 June the OCR pass had produced
477,284 accepted records from 3,571 works, about 183M tokens.
blocks.zh:
从五月下旬到六月下旬,我们收集了第一件尸体: 泰米尔语网络爬行( FineWeb-2,
HPLT, Sangraha)和泰米尔语书籍的文本出自泰米尔语BooksPDF和Archive.org. 许多印有泰米尔文的文字只存在于扫描器中
图片,所以我们运行魔方 OCR 在泰米尔数字图书馆 和扫描的部分 泰米尔 BooksPDF 收藏。 截至6月17日,OCR通行证已经制作
477,284个接受来自3,571个作品的记录,约183M个信使.

blocks.en:
Getting a run to finish took longer than designing it. From 30 June our attempts on rented
8 × \times H200 nodes failed on communication timeouts between GPUs and on resuming from checkpoints. After three weeks we
stopped retrying, rewrote the launch process and moved to Lambda. The production run started on 24 July 2026: 1.56B
parameters and 30B tokens on 8 × \times H100. Its node shut itself down before the final checkpoint was copied off, so the
last 4,221 steps had to be redone from an earlier checkpoint. Four rounds of continued pretraining followed, bringing
the model’s total training to about 66B tokens.

8\times H200节点在GPU之间的通讯超时和从检查站恢复时失败. 三个星期后,我们
停止了重试,重制了发射过程并搬到了Lambda. 2026年7月24日开工生产:1.56B.

最后4 221个步骤不得不从先前的检查站重开。 随后进行了四轮持续预训,带来了
该模型的总训练达到大约66B个符号。

blocks.en:
We then spent two months on post-training: SFT on a few thousand pairs, a fix for a wrong stop
token, two runs of direct preference optimisation (DPO, which trains a model to prefer a chosen reply over a rejected
one) that reached 96% preference accuracy and transferred nothing, an abstention patch, a run of group relative policy
optimisation (GRPO, a reinforcement-learning method that scores several sampled replies against each other) on taste
ratings, a 145,000-row SFT scale-up, safety and character runs, and finally SFT on native Tamil conversations. The
scale-up taught us something specific: its general instruction corpora made the model copy passages, and a Qwen2.5-1.5B
control trained on the same data copied too, which pointed to the data rather than to our model. We
released the model privately to the volunteers on 18 September 2026; it was never made public.

收视率,14.5万行的SFT扩展,安全和人物运行,最后SFT在泰米尔本土对话上. 这个
扩大教育告诉我们一些具体内容: 公司的一般指示 复制了模型的段落, 和一个Quen2.5-1.5B

Graded by the same judge and prompts we later used for the new model, the first

blocks.en: 3.1 A tokenizer that keeps line breaks
blocks.zh: 3.1 国家 保存换行符的标识器

blocks.en:
The first model’s tokenizer (TOK_BPE_64K, a SentencePiece BPE) ran a normaliser that collapsed every run of whitespace
into one space. Newlines and indentation never reached the model: a sample of 150M training tokens contained no newline
token, and the chat stop marker never appeared in pretraining (Section 2 ).
Without line breaks and indentation a model cannot represent verse, multi-line lists or indentation-sensitive code
faithfully, and it never sees the stop marker that ends a chat turn, so the second model needed a new tokenizer before
it needed anything else.

符号,聊天停止标记从未在预训中出现(第2节).
没有换行和缩进, 模型不能代表诗句、 多行列表或缩进敏感代码
所以第二款型号需要新的代号

blocks.en:
We compared two candidates, with the evaluation prompts and held-out texts excluded from their training text by hash and
substring: a byte-level BPE in the Hugging Face tokenizers library, trained on a 930M-character sample (Tamil
58.0%, English 29.0%, code 5.6%, chat and tool text 4.3%, Tanglish 3.0%, parallel 0.1%), and a SentencePiece BPE
with whitespace preserved, trained on half of that sample. Both learn their vocabulary the same way, by repeatedly merging the most frequent pair of adjacent pieces into
a new token; they differ in what they start from. A byte-level BPE starts from the 256 possible bytes, so it can encode
any text, while SentencePiece starts from characters and must fall back to raw bytes for characters it has not seen.
Both have 64,000 ids and round-trip every test set exactly. We chose the byte-level BPE (TOK_FRESH_20260924). It
matched SentencePiece on Tamil and was better on code, Tanglish, JSON and chat, and it never needs a fallback, where
SentencePiece used 2,257 fallback tokens on code. A byte-level BPE trained on the same half sample as
SentencePiece came within 0.01 tokens per word of the full one, so the difference comes from the algorithm, not the
amount of training text.

blocks.en:
The pre-tokenizer is Qwen2’s split pattern with one change. In Qwen2 the class of characters that make up a word is
Unicode letters only ( \p{L} ); ours also admits combining marks ( \p{M} ) and the two zero-width joiners,
U+200C and U+200D. Tamil vowel signs are combining marks, so with letters alone every Tamil word is split at each vowel
sign. We expect this is part of why Qwen2.5 spends 9.4 tokens per Tamil word on our samples (Table 2 ),
alongside its English-heavy vocabulary, but we did not train a tokenizer without the change to measure its share. There is no
normaliser; the pack builder applies Unicode NFC before tokenization.

只使用 Unicode 字母 (\p{L} ); 我们的也承认结合了标记 (\p{M}) 和两个零宽连接符,
U+200C和U+200D.  U. 泰米尔语元音符号正在合并标记,所以单用字母,每个泰米尔语单词在每一个元音中被分出.
签名。 我们期望这是Quen2.5为何在我们的样本上每泰米尔字花9.4个符号的一部分(表2)。
但是我们没有训练一个标语器, 没有
normaliser; 包构建器在符号化前应用了 Unicode NFC.

blocks.en:
On Tamil prose the new tokenizer is no cheaper than the old one (1.55 tokens per word for both); what it adds is an
exact round trip, line breaks included, and cheaper Tanglish, code, JSON and chat. Two costs came with the change. Verse became more expensive (2.29 against 1.80 tokens per word): the tokenizer sample
held only 0.3% classical text. And 14.3% of Tamil token boundaries fall inside a grapheme cluster, against 4.7% for the
old tokenizer; no boundary falls inside a UTF-8 character. We did not measure what the grapheme splits cost the model.
Romanized Tamil costs 1.67 times as many tokens as the same sentence in Tamil script (2.71 times with the old tokenizer).

旧符号; UTF-8 字符内没有边界 。 我们没有测量石墨的分化 使模型付出的代价。
罗马化的泰米尔语与同句泰米尔语同句相差1.67倍(与"老"的同句相差2.71倍).

blocks.en:
Ids 0–7 are special: end of text (0), the chat markers <|im_start|> and <|im_end|> (1, 2), tool-call
and tool-response delimiters (3–6) and padding (7); ids 8–27 are reserved. In pretraining every document is encoded
with special-token parsing switched off and closed with one end-of-text token. Chat transcripts in pretraining are plain
text with User: / Assistant: lines, so the model learns turn structure from text, while the special
markers are reserved for SFT, where <|im_end|> is the stop token.

blocks.en: 3.2 Pretraining corpus

blocks.en:
The pack holds 39.39B unique tokens from 68 sources, drawn to 50B training tokens with repeats: 43.5B in the stable
stage, which uses 63 of the sources, and 6.5B in the decay stage, which uses 27 (Section 4 ).
Table 3 gives the planned shares by category, and Figure 3 the stable-stage mix by source. Tamil is the majority, but measured Tamil supply is the binding
constraint: after near-duplicate removal the native Tamil web, books, OCR and curated text came to 16–19B tokens, not the
45B we had first estimated, so Tamil sources are repeated up to four times while English, math and code
fill the rest.

blocks.en:
The Tamil side includes three OCR passes over printed books: the first model’s Tesseract pass over the Tamil Digital
Library, an indic-ocr pass over 976 PDFs (142,271 pages) and a Sarvam re-OCR of 358 books (59,841 pages). In the
first model, damaged OCR text, not the model, explained several failures, and an OCR filter that we had judged only by
how rarely it fired on clean text turned out to throw away good Tamil 37 times out of 41 (Section 2 ). A
filter has to be judged by what it removes, so the OCR rules for this corpus are narrow and each was checked by reading
its rejects:
pages with runaway repetition are cut or dropped, scan watermarks, empty table markup and picture descriptions are
removed, documents in legacy font encodings or with interleaved two-column text are dropped, and where an OCR book and
a web or e-text copy hold the same text, the cleaner copy is kept. OCR-derived text is a small part of the result:
about 1.8% of stable-stage tokens and 0.9% of decay-stage tokens.

泰米尔一侧包括三个OCR通过印刷书籍:第一个模型的魔方通过泰米尔数字
图书馆,一个Indic-ocr传出976个PDF(142,271页)和一个Sarvam再传出358个图书(59,841页). 在那个
第一个模型,损坏的OCR文本,而不是模型,解释了几个故障,一个OCR过滤器,我们只通过
在41起事件中, A级
过滤器需要通过它去除什么来判断, 所以这个体格的OCR规则是狭义的,每个都通过读取来检查
拒绝:
重复运行的页面被剪切或丢弃、扫描水印、空表标记和图片描述
删除,删除遗留字体编码中或带有相隔两栏文字的文档,并删除 OCR 书和
网页或电子文本副本持有相同的文本,清洁文本保存。 OCR衍生出的案文是结果的一小部分:
约1.8%的稳定相和0.9%的衰变相相.

blocks.en:
Licences decide admission. Public datasets are used if they are on Hugging Face under an open licence; the six NVIDIA
datasets are used for training only and are never redistributed. The rest is Tamil text we collected ourselves: books,
e-texts and the OCR passes above. Section 7.2 records the material whose terms differ from our release
licence (two public instruction sets and two OCR tools) and how we chose the release licence. Frontier models (Claude, Codex, GPT, Gemini) planned the work and
wrote code. Under our rule they may write the user side of a training conversation but not the assistant replies the
model learns from; the replies we generated (Section 3.4 ) come from open-weight teacher models.
Section 7.2 lists where frontier-model text did enter, including public datasets that frontier models
produced upstream. Every new training source was scanned against the evaluation prompts before it was admitted.
blocks.zh:
许可决定录取。 公共数据集如果在公开许可证下的Hugging Face上使用; 6 NVIDIA
数据集仅用于培训,从未重新分配。 其余的是我们自己收集的泰米尔文:书籍,
e-text和OCR通过以上。 第7.2节记录了与我们公布内容不同的材料
许可证(两套公共指示和两套OCR工具)以及我们如何选择释放许可证。 边疆模型(克洛德、Codex、GPT、双子座)规划了这项工作和
写出代码。 根据我们的规则,他们可以写培训对话的用户方,但助理不能回答
模式从中汲取教训;我们生成的答复(第3.4节)来自开放式教师模式。

Pretraining ends with a decay stage, in which the learning rate falls to a tenth of its peak
(Section 4.2 ). Recent open models give their highest-quality data to this final stage [ 25 ] , and we did the same: the decay stage changes the mix as well as the learning rate
(Figure 4 ). It keeps 22 of the stable stage’s 63 sources, adds five new ones,
and moves weight from broad web crawls (CulturaX, HPLT, OSCAR, MADLAD-400, a second Sangraha cut) to curated and
higher-quality text: FineWeb2 Tamil rises from 9.2% to 25.8% of tokens, Sangraha-verified from 1.0% to 6.8%,
Project Madurai from 0.2% to 1.4%, FineMath-4+ from 3.7% to 12.3% and FineWeb-Edu (score ≥ \geq 4) from 2.9% to
10.8%. Five task and instruction sources appear only in decay, together about 23% of its tokens: passage tasks,
Tanglish, formatting, tool use and translation in plain-text chat form (Section 3.1 ).
One of them, a pool of earlier instruction data, includes Tamil translations of SmolTalk’s constraint-following
conversations, whose instruction templates are IFEval’s; Section 7 reports what that does to one
benchmark.

memorised text. The second model ends every document with an end-of-text token, and we split each sample at those tokens and pass it to the attention kernel as a packed batch with per-document offsets, so each document attends only
to itself, rotary positions restart at each document, and flash attention stays on.

blocks.en:
Training used a warmup–stable–decay schedule in two runs (Table 4 ; loss and learning rate in

at the end. Unlike a cosine schedule, this does not fix the length of the run in advance: any checkpoint of the stable
stage can be finished with a short decay. Both runs use 524,288 tokens per
optimizer step: the decay stage doubles the context and halves the number of sequences per step. The decay run starts
from the last stable checkpoint, weights and optimizer state, and lowers the learning rate linearly to a tenth of the
peak while switching to the decay mix (Section 3.3 ). The optimizer is Adam with β = ( 0.9 , 0.95 ) \beta=(0.9,0.95) ,

eight GPUs (NeMo 2 on Megatron-Core [ 14 , 22 ] ).

blocks.en:
This was our one chance to train this model: the run used most of the available compute credits, and
there was no budget to repeat it. The first model had lost its final checkpoint when its node shut itself down before
the checkpoint was copied off (Section 2 ). The operating setup for this run was built around that failure:

检查站被抄走(第2节)。 这次运行的操作设置是围绕这次失败而构建的:

checkpoint every two hours. It first hard-linked the checkpoint on the node, since the framework renames its latest
checkpoint at each save, then copied it with six parallel streams (33 GB in 36–56 minutes) and kept it only after a
second pass found nothing left to transfer. A second process archived a copy every 10,000 steps, plus the end of each
stage, to a local disk. The per-step metrics, validation records and logs were copied with every checkpoint. • The node releases itself only after the final copy. After training, the node waited for a marker that the
copier writes only once the final checkpoint and run records are safe, then terminated its own instance. A stage failure
would hold the node for two hours for inspection. Two hard deadlines, one on the node and one on a local PC,
capped the spend regardless. • Monitoring with a record. A check ran every hour for the first day and every two hours after that: step,
throughput, loss and validation trend, GPU use and disk, the cloud instance, the guards, the copies, and the SHA-256
hashes of the data files, which matched the launch baseline at every check. Each check appended a line to a heartbeat
file in the repository, and a scheduled cloud job alerted by e-mail if that file went stale.

blocks.en: 5 The base model

blocks.en:
All base-model numbers in this section come from one harness, the EleutherAI evaluation harness [ 9 ] with the same task definitions and settings for every model, on full test sets unless
stated. Translation is scored with chrF [ 16 ] , which compares the output with the reference
translation in character sequences rather than whole words; this suits Tamil, where one word carries several suffixes and
a near-miss should earn partial credit. Translation prompts are 5-shot: five example translations precede the sentence.
Multiple-choice tasks are scored by log-likelihood: the model does not write an answer, and instead we compare the
probability it assigns to each option and count the most probable one as its choice (length-normalised for ARC and
HellaSwag). We compare against Sarvam-1 [ 19 ] , a 2B
Indic base model; our previous model, the \tamilfont அகரம் / Agaram 1.5B base; and, where the earlier run covered them, Qwen2.5-1.5B and
Gemma-3-1B instruction-tuned models evaluated the same way [ 18 , 10 ] .

compare across checkpoints and across models with different tokenizers.

blocks.en:
Every register improved through the stable stage and again in decay. The literary EPUB register dropped much further
in decay than the others, so we checked it for leakage. The decay stage reads only from the pack the held-out scan
covered, including the five sources used only in decay. The gain is broad: 98% of the passages improved, the passages
with no overlap at all improved more (median 11.1%) than those with some (9.6%), and 25 of the 29 books gained at least
5%. The passages themselves did not leak. The books did, in part: when the held-out set was built, the clean text of
these books was found in the training pack, and the held-out passages are the ones that individually do not overlap it.
The decay mix also upweighted the sources that hold those books (Section 3.3 ). We therefore read the EPUB
number as performance on unseen passages of partly seen books, not as generalisation to new literature; the other four
registers are the cleaner measure.

blocks.en: 6 Supervised fine-tuning
blocks.zh: 6 监督微调

blocks.en: 6.1 Training
blocks.zh: 6.1 培训

blocks.en:
We fine-tuned the final base model on the SFT set of Section 3.4 (134,428 training conversations) for
three epochs: full fine-tuning, loss on assistant turns only, sequences up to 8,192 tokens packed to 65,536 tokens per
step (758 steps per epoch, 2,274 in total), learning rate 2 × 10 − 5 2\times 10^{-5} with 3% warmup and cosine decay, AdamW,
gradient clipping at 1.0, bf16. Loss on assistant turns only means the model is trained to write the replies, not to
predict what users say; packing places several conversations in one sequence so no compute is spent on padding. A
checkpoint was kept at the end of every epoch. Training took 9.5 hours on one H200
(JarvisLabs) at about 15 seconds per step.
A first attempt on a rented H100 PCIe ran at 37 seconds per step because the GPU was thermally throttled (87–89 ∘ C,
software thermal slowdown active); at that pace it could not finish inside its spend guard, so we stopped it after
3.7 hours and moved the run.

After training we measured each checkpoint on held-out SFT data and generated its replies to our evaluation prompts. The validation loss on the 2,736 held-out SFT conversations fell from 1.416 for the base model to 1.096 after epoch 1 and 1.093 after epochs 2 and 3:
almost all of the change happened in the first epoch, and it did not rise afterwards (Table 7 ). Each epoch
then answered both open-chat evaluation sets with greedy decoding.

blocks.en: 6.2 Evaluation
blocks.zh: 6.2 评价

blocks.en:
The open-chat sets are 248 prompts written by hand by a native Tamil speaker on our team: 100 in the first set (open questions, explanation,
everyday advice, Thirukkural and classical text, Tanglish, code-switching, multi-turn follow-ups, “don’t know”
questions and safety) and 148 in the second, which adds tool calls, identity questions, format constraints and
creative writing. Every prompt has a reference answer; the second set’s tool prompts carry the expected call and are
scored by exact match. Section 7 reports their overlap with training data.
blocks.zh:
开场白是248个提示, 由本团队的泰米尔语母语代表手写: 第一组100个(开场白,解释,
每日建议,Thirukkural和古典文本,Tanglish,代码切换,多回合跟踪,“不知道”
第二行第148个,增加了工具呼叫、身份问题、格式限制和
创意写作. 每个提示都有参考答案;第二集的工具提示带有预期的呼叫,而且
得分准确的匹配。 第7节报告它们与培训数据重叠。

blocks.en:
We score replies three ways. Format checks are scripted: the reply stops on its own, does not loop or echo the
prompt, and is in the right script. A judge , a large language model asked to grade replies, does what three
people cannot do for every checkpoint: read hundreds of replies each time. Ours (Kimi K3, temperature 0) grades each
reply blind against a frozen rubric as usable or not; usable means correct, in the right script, complete and stopped, and a multi-turn conversation
is usable only if every turn is. The judge sees six models’ replies per prompt in shuffled order, three of them earlier
models whose grades we already had; it reproduced those grades (2, 3 and 6 out of 100), and two passes over the same
replies agreed on 88–90% of items. And people compared the two leading checkpoints blind (Section 6.3 ).

我们得到的回答有三种方式。 格式检查是脚本:回复会自行停止,不会循环或回放

模式,我们已有的分数;它复制了这些分数(100分中的2分、3分和6分),两个通过同样的分数
答复商定88-90%的项目。 人们把两个主要检查站比作盲人(第6.3节)。

blocks.en:
Fine-tuning turned a base model that rarely stopped (15% of replies) into a chat model that stops almost always and
writes in the user’s script. Against the earlier models on the same judge it is a different class: about half of its
replies are judged usable, against 2 of 100 for the \tamilfont அகரம் / Agaram 1.5B release model and 3 for the mid-run SFT on the
step-21K base, and multi-turn conversations are usable for the first time (4–6 of 15, against none before). Tool use
moved the most between the mid-run test and the final model: the right tool 96% of the time, with exactly the right
arguments 60%, against 56% and 16% at step 55K. The format checks overstate quality: they pass 94–95% of replies
the judge passes only about half of, because they cannot see wrong facts.

微调将很少停止(15%的答复)的基数模型转变为聊天模式,几乎总是停止

在中跑测试和最终模式之间移动最多:96%的时间是合适的工具,完全正确
60%,56%和16%在55K级。 格式检查质量过重:它们通过了94-95%的答复

blocks.en:
On instruction following in Tamil, the native-Tamil IndicIFEval subset nearly doubled over the base model, from 10.0%
to 18.6–19.3%, ahead of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (11.2%) in our harness. The translated subset fell after SFT, from 19.6%
to 16–17%; Section 7 explains why the base model’s score there may not measure what it seems to.
IndicIFEval checks whether a reply obeys verifiable constraints such as a word count, a required keyword or a format;
a prompt passes under the strict score only if every constraint is met exactly, and the loose score relaxes the
checks, for example by ignoring markdown and a leading or trailing line.

严格分数下的快速通过 只有当每个限制都得到了准确的满足 和松散分数放松
检查,例如忽略了标记下和一条前行或后行。

blocks.en: 6.4 What fine-tuning did not fix
blocks.zh: 6.4 (中文(简体) ). 什么微调没有解决

blocks.en: Reading the replies found four failures that the scores alone hide.
blocks.zh: 阅读这些答复后发现四个失败,单是得分就隐藏了这些失败.

blocks.en:
The SFT set held 976 identity conversations, but those we read pair one fixed question with one
fixed answer. The model learned fragments, not facts: epoch 1 gave its name as “ \tamilfont அ”, epoch 3 as “Anamika”, and
both agreed when a user asserted they were a fine-tune of Llama, which this model is not.
blocks.zh:
SFT集共进行了976次身份对话, 但那些我们读到一个固定问题和一个
固定的答案。 模型学到了碎片,而不是事实:纪元1将其取名为“\tamilfont QQ”,纪元3取名为“Anamika”,以及
双方都同意,当一个用户声称他们是Llama的微调,而这个模式并非如此。

blocks.en:
Of the five safety prompts in the first set, the judge passed one reply from epoch 1
and none from epoch 3. Both epochs gave practical tips for cheating in an exam, attempted made-up steps to disable
security logs, and, asked for an anonymous threat, refused and then offered to write it if given details. A probe of ten
distress messages written by a volunteer found warm, script-matched replies to mild distress, but the severe cases were
handled inconsistently: neither epoch gave a helpline to a user describing thoughts of self-harm, and only epoch 1 told a
user who said they were not safe to call the national emergency number. The helpline number the crisis data taught
(Tele-MANAS, 14416) appeared, correctly, but in replies to moderate distress rather than the severe cases.

The model can call lookup tools and answer from what they return; 12,647 SFT
conversations train that loop. But in every one of them the returned text was relevant. When we connected a simple
Wikipedia lookup and gave the model the top result for each question, the result was off-topic for four of five
questions (keyword search on Tamil questions picks up verb forms, not topics), and the model paraphrased the off-topic
text as its answer in all four, describing a chess rule in reply to a question about why idli batter rises.

维基百科查找并给模型 每一个问题的顶端结果, 结果是非主题的 四五
问题(泰米尔语问题的关键词搜索取出动词形式,而不是专题),模型将非专题化
文本作为它在所有四个中的答案,描述一个围棋规则,以回答一个关于idli击球手为什么会起跑的问题.

Many unusable replies are fluent and wrong: why birds on a power line are not shocked, why soil smells
before rain. These come from the base model’s knowledge, which fine-tuning does not add (Section 5.2 ).

blocks.en: 6.5 Three targeted rounds
blocks.zh: 6.5 (中文(简体) ). 三发定点弹

blocks.en:
We tried to fix those failures with three short SFT rounds, each starting from the previous round’s chosen checkpoint
(Table 8 ). The method was the same each time. We read the failing replies and wrote a list of scenarios
for each failure, such as a user insisting that the model is a Llama fine-tune, a casual request for an exam-cheating
trick, or a distress message that asks the assistant to keep it secret. Gemma-4-31B, an open-weight model served on
the two DGX Spark machines, wrote the conversations. Scripted validators rejected rows that broke a rule for their area,
for example a crisis reply without the Tele-MANAS number (14416) in its opening sentences, a refusal that opened with
“sure”, or an identity reply that named another model’s maker without denying it. New rows were mixed with rows
replayed from the previous round’s set (61–73% of each set) so that general chat would not drift. All three rounds ran
on one DGX Spark at about 131 seconds per step, with the same trainer and learning rate as the first SFT stage.

例如,在开句中没有Tele-MANAS号码(14416)的危机答复,这一拒绝以下列方式开启:
" 确定 " 或身份答复,在不否认的情况下,指定了另一个模型的制造者。 新行与行相混合
从上一回合的组合(每集61–73%)重放,这样一般聊天就不会漂移. 三发子弹都跑掉了
一个DGX Spark每步约131秒,教练和学习率与SFT第一阶段相同.

blocks.en: 7 Contamination

blocks.en:
A Tamil web crawl contains translated Wikipedia, news and exam material, so benchmark text can reach a training corpus
without anyone adding it. The first model taught us to check this before reporting a number (Section 2 ).
For each evaluation set in Table 9 we measured, item by item, the fraction of its 13-token windows (in
our tokenizer) that occur anywhere in the 68 files of the training pack. We report scores on the full test sets, and
for translation also on the pairs whose overlap is below 5%. Four benchmarks we report (XCOPA, HellaSwag, INCLUDE and
MultiBLiMP) were not scanned; Section 10 lists them. A run of 13 consecutive tokens is long enough that a match is unlikely to happen by chance, and
short enough to catch a sentence copied inside a longer document. For translation pairs, an item is clean only if both sides are.

IndicIFEval [ 13 ] has two Tamil subsets:
prompts written natively in Tamil and prompts translated from IFEval [ 28 ] . No prompt of either subset is
in our pack. But in the translated subset the shared text is the instruction itself, for example “at least 3

stage used at 3.4% of its tokens; 2,411 pool rows contain the placeholder instruction alone. SmolTalk’s constraint data
was built with “detailed constraints similar to the ones found in IFEval” and then decontaminated against IFEval with a
10-gram filter [ 3 ] . That filter removes IFEval’s prompts but keeps its instruction templates, which
IFEval reuses across many prompts with different numbers. Our decay stage therefore trained on Tamil versions of the
templates the translated subset tests. None of these rows are in the SFT set.

anyone, including for commercial work, but we will choose the licence only after the two companies reply and legal
review is complete; until then the weights are published without a licence. The release carries a NOTICE file that
names this material.

blocks.en: 8.2 Chat quality
blocks.zh: 8.2 国家 聊天质量

blocks.en:
The first two prompt sets helped choose what the targeted rounds trained on and which
checkpoint to release (Section 7.1 ), so we wrote a third. On 11 October 2026, after the release
checkpoint was chosen, we wrote 50 new prompts by hand, each with a reference answer: 40 open questions
and 10 two-turn conversations, 30 in Tanglish and 20 in Tamil script. They cover everyday and school-level facts,
polite phrasing and short follow-ups: what to use to erase a pencil mistake, how many slippers make a pair, why birds
build nests, how to ask a shopkeeper for a price. The set was frozen before any reply was generated and has not been
used to choose data or checkpoints.
blocks.zh:
前两套快速装置帮助选择了所训练的有目标的子弹和
因此我们写了第三个。 2026年10月11日,在释放后
检查点被选中,我们用手写出50个新的提示,每个提示都有参考答案:40个未解问题
和10个两回合的对话, 30个在唐利什语, 20个在泰米尔文。 它们涵盖了日常和学校层面的事实,
礼貌的用词和简短的后继:用什么来消除铅笔出错,多少拖鞋制造一对,为什么鸟类
筑起巢穴,如何向店主索取出价. 在得到任何答复之前,该套设备已被冻结,目前尚未
用于选择数据或检查站。

blocks.en:
The judge (Kimi K3 through the Fireworks API, the same rubric as the first set) graded the released
model’s replies three times, each pass in a freshly shuffled blind pool with three other checkpoints. It judged 23, 22
and 24 of the 50 replies usable, a mean of 23.0 (46%); 48 of the 50 items got the same verdict in all three passes. By
type the mean is 9.7 of 20 single-turn Tanglish prompts, 9.0 of 20 single-turn Tamil-script prompts and 4.3 of 10
two-turn conversations. Almost every failure is a wrong answer, not a formatting failure. In the first pass, 26 of the
27 unusable replies were marked factually wrong, and all but one stopped cleanly in the right script. Two examples:
asked what to use to erase a pencil mistake, the model suggests the Undo key, and asked how many slippers are in a pair,
it answers 12. The replies are fluent Tanglish or Tamil; the content is what fails.

模特儿回答三次, 判决23、22

类型中,平均值为:20个单转Tanglish 提示的9.7个;20个单转泰米尔语提示的9.0个;10个的4.3个。
两个回合的对话。 几乎所有的失败都是错误的答案,而不是格式化的失败. 在第一次传球中,26名
27个无法使用的答复在事实上有明显错误,除了一个以外,所有答复都以正确的文字完全停止。 有两个例子:
问用什么来抹去铅笔错误 模型建议使用 Undo 键 问一对里有多少拖鞋
答复是流利的唐来语或泰米尔语;内容是失败的。

blocks.en:
The first prompt set shows how much a single judge pass can move. The round-4 pass
judged 57 of the released model’s 100 replies usable. A re-pass over the identical reply file judged 46, with 13
verdicts flipped (12 of them from usable to not usable, all borderline answers the judge had first accepted as loose but
acceptable). Two more passes gave 49 and 52. Over four passes the mean is 51.0, and 18 of the 100 items did not get the
same verdict in the three later passes. Agreement on the 50 short questions of the third set is higher (48 of 50
unanimous) than on the first set, which has longer and multi-turn items. We therefore report chat quality as a mean over
passes with its range, and treat differences under about 5 points on a 100-item set as noise. Long multi-turn items
can also break the judge itself: in two passes Kimi K3 spent its whole 8,000-token reply budget reasoning and wrote no
verdict for 21 such items, which we regraded with a 24,000-token budget.

blocks.en: 11 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 11 结论

blocks.en:
We trained a Tamil–English chat model from scratch, as a team of three; its pretraining run cost about USD 4,765 in
rented compute, and the whole project, across both models, about USD 13,300 (Section 9 ). It writes
fluent Tamil and Tanglish, translates better than Sarvam-1, follows about a fifth of native-Tamil constraint
instructions exactly and calls tools on schemas it has seen in training, but it answers only about half of everyday
questions acceptably, and nearly every failure is a wrong fact. Neither of our two extra SFT experiments improved the
knowledge measures; they changed how the model answers. We suspect the limit is pretraining, 50B tokens against the trillions of larger models,
but we have not tested whether more pretraining, particularly on more Tamil text, would fix it.
blocks.zh:
我们作为一个三人小组,从零开始培训泰米尔-英语聊天模式;其预训费用约为4,765美元。
租用的计算和整个项目,在两种模型中,大约为13,300美元(第9节)。 它写着
与Sarvam-1相比,
准确的指令 并调用工具 它在训练中看到的计划, 但是它只回答 大约一半的日常
几乎每一次失败都是错误的事实。 我们两次额外的SFT实验都没有改进过
知识计量;它们改变了模型的答案。 我们怀疑限制是预先训练,50B的代币 相对于数以万亿计的大型模型,
但是,我们还没有测试更多的预先训练,特别是对更多的泰米尔文本的预先训练,是否会纠正它。

blocks.en:
For a team that picks this up, three things should carry over. First, the constraint we hit was Tamil text: after
near-duplicate removal there were 16–19B tokens of native Tamil, so the run had to repeat them several times. Finding
more clean Tamil, from books, archives and public institutions, is where we would put the next effort. Second, the
evaluation method costs little and caught most of our mistakes: prompts written by native speakers after the training
data is fixed, scans of evaluation sets against the training data, judge verdicts read
against replies and repeated over several passes, and a person deciding between close checkpoints. Third, the setup
for running one large job safely on a rented node (Section 4.3 ) meant the run finished once, on
budget, with nothing lost.

blocks.en:
We release the base and chat models as safetensors and as GGUF files for llama.cpp [ 11 ] , each at
16-bit, 8-bit ( Q8_0 , 2.69 GB) and 4-bit ( Q4_K_M , 1.56 GB) precision. llama.cpp has no entry for
our pre-tokenizer, so the files use its closest match, qwen35 , which differs only in leaving out the zero-width
joiners (U+200C, U+200D). llama.cpp’s token ids matched the Hugging Face tokenizer on all 961 test texts (our three chat
evaluation sets and 300 held-out training conversations), though none of them contains a zero-width joiner. On greedy
replies to 8 held-out prompts, the 16-bit chat file matched the Hugging Face model character for character on 7, the
8-bit file on 5 and the 4-bit file on 1, so we recommend the 8-bit file or larger. The files need llama.cpp build b11574
or later.

At the time of writing, the release contains the weights and tokenizer
of both models, the GGUF files with their conversion script and parity check, the chat script and the model cards. It
does not contain the training corpus or the pretraining pack, which mix sources whose licences do not all allow
redistribution (the NVIDIA datasets may be used for training but not redistributed); the training, tokenizer and
data-pipeline code; the source manifests and filter rules; the evaluation harness configuration; the contamination
scan; our three chat prompt sets, their reference answers and tool schemas; or the judge rubric, replies and verdicts.
This report gives the settings needed to rebuild each of these: the architecture and optimiser
(Section 4 ), the tokenizer sample and pre-tokenizer (Section 3.1 ), the sources and
their shares (Section 3 ), the evaluation settings (Section 5 ) and the scan method
(Section 7 ).

blocks.en:
Ramchand Kumaresan led the project: data collection and the corpus, the tokenizer, both pretraining runs, fine-tuning
and evaluation. He wrote all 298 chat evaluation prompts by hand (the reference answers and expected tool calls of the
second set were drafted with Kimi, two of them with Claude, as guidance for the judge), marked about half of the
2,086 rows in the review sheets for the first model (OCR and filter review, judge calibration, SFT correctness, safety,
pairwise comparisons), and compared the two leading SFT checkpoints blind. Madhusudhanan G and Kaushik Kezendirane tested and graded both
models: their tests of the first model traced its free-chat failure to unseparated documents, measured long-context
recall over 75 generations and set a literary-quality gate on which they agreed on 35 of 40 items; for the second model
a volunteer wrote the distress probe, and a volunteer repeated the blind checkpoint comparison with AI assistance. AI assistants
(Claude and Codex) wrote code and helped plan the work, Kimi K3 served as the judge, and open-weight models wrote the
generated training replies.
